newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-HILL UNDER ATTACK FROM ALL SIDES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL UNDER ATTACK FROM ALL SIDES.

text.p: Damon Hill will undergo the most critical examination of his career at the Italian Grand Prix this weekend.
The Briton's shock axing by Williams and the presence of Michael Schumacher's winning Ferrari on home territory are two huge obstacles blocking his path to the world championship.
Worries over whether Williams will fulfil their promise of 100 percent support or instead lean towards his settled and focused team mate Jacques Villeneuve add to the pressure.
Hill's series of poor starts in recent races complete what seems a pessimistic picture.
But the British driver's iron will to succeed against overwhelming odds -- a legacy handed down by his late father Graham -- could tip the scales back in his favour.
He leads the series by 13 points with three races left and knows full well that Villeneuve must challenge him for the crown, not the other way around.
In fact, a Hill victory and a non-podium finish by his Canadian rival will settle the championship.
Hill, expected to give his version of the split with his team later on Thursday, said: "I am looking at it as a new opportunity, a fresh challenge.
"It gives me a chance to prove myself again and I am keen, more than anything, to show what I can do in the three races remaining this season.
"It is not what you would describe as a comfortable lead but it's a lead that I am grateful to have and the fewer races there are left the better shape I am in, I think."
Hill won the Italian Grand Prix in 1993 and 1994 but crashed out last year in a collision with Schumacher.
Schumacher took his Ferrari to a brilliant victory in Belgium two weeks ago. Morale is high at last in the team and, as usual, much is expected of them on the fast and famous circuit.
The reigning champion tried to play down expectations of him claiming his first victory on Italian soil since he joined Ferrari.
"I am not certain that our car is totally suited to the circuit and I feel we are not yet totally reliable either," he warned.
McLaren and Benetton should also be strong players this weekend as their cars have performed increasingly well on the high-speed circuits.
For Benetton pair, Jean Alesi and Gerhard Berger, the race is also their first return to Monza since leaving Ferrari -- an extra source of motivation to succeed.
